propositions.name: consciousness_distinguishes_temporal_phases
propositions.statement: Consciousness distinguishes present sensation from remembrance of past sensations and anticipation of future sensations.
propositions.quote: we distinguish without difficulty present sensation from the remembrance of past sensations or the anticipation of future sensations

propositions.name: conscious_phenomena_have_temporal_order
propositions.statement: Of two conscious phenomena which we remember, one was anterior to the other.
propositions.quote: we know perfectly well what we mean when we say that of two conscious phenomena which we remember, one was anterior to the other

propositions.name: simultaneity_of_conscious_facts
propositions.statement: Two conscious facts are simultaneous when they profoundly interpenetrate so that analysis can not separate them without mutilating them.
propositions.quote: we mean that they profoundly interpenetrate, so that analysis can not separate them without mutilating them

propositions.name: order_of_conscious_phenomena_not_arbitrary
propositions.statement: The order in which we arrange conscious phenomena does not admit of any arbitrariness; it is imposed upon us and of it we can change nothing.
propositions.quote: The order in which we arrange conscious phenomena does not admit of any arbitrariness. It is imposed upon us and of it we can change nothing.

propositions.name: memory_requires_loss_of_actuality
propositions.statement: For a sensation to become a remembrance classified in time, it must have ceased to be actual and lost the sense of its infinite complexity.
propositions.quote: it must have ceased to be actual, we must have lost the sense of its infinite complexity, otherwise it would have remained present

propositions.name: finite_labels_yield_discontinuous_psychologic_time
propositions.statement: Because the labels around which memories crystallize can only be finite in number, psychologic time should be discontinuous.
propositions.quote: these labels can only be finite in number. On that score, psychologic time should be discontinuous.

propositions.name: time_is_form_preexistent_in_mind
propositions.statement: Time is a form pre-existent in our minds.
propositions.quote: How could that be, if time were not a form pre-existent in our minds?

propositions.name: physical_facts_populate_space_unseen
propositions.statement: Physical facts are things with which we people space and which no consciousness sees directly.
propositions.quote: we wish to put there physical facts, these I know not what with which we people space and which no consciousness sees directly

propositions.name: psychologic_time_gives_rise_to_physical_time
propositions.statement: Psychologic time is given to us and must needs create scientific and physical time.
propositions.quote: psychologic time is given to us and must needs create scientific and physical time

propositions.name: consciousnesses_are_impenetrable_worlds
propositions.statement: Two consciousnesses are like two worlds impenetrable one to the other.
propositions.quote: Think of two consciousnesses, which are like two worlds impenetrable one to the other.

propositions.name: no_direct_intuition_of_equal_durations
propositions.statement: We have not a direct intuition of the equality of two intervals of time.
propositions.quote: We have not a direct intuition of the equality of two intervals of time

propositions.name: pendulum_beats_defined_equal
propositions.statement: To measure time, physicists use the pendulum and suppose by definition that all the beats of this pendulum are of equal duration.
propositions.quote: To measure time they use the pendulum and they suppose by definition that all the beats of this pendulum are of equal duration.

propositions.name: pendulum_pace_varies_with_physical_causes
propositions.statement: The temperature, the resistance of the air, the barometric pressure, make the pace of the pendulum vary.
propositions.quote: the temperature, the resistance of the air, the barometric pressure, make the pace of the pendulum vary

propositions.name: sidereal_day_as_unit_of_time
propositions.statement: It is supposed that two complete rotations of the earth about its axis have the same duration, making the sidereal day the constant unit of time.
propositions.quote: two complete rotations of the earth about its axis have the same duration

propositions.name: earth_rotation_slowing_from_tides
propositions.statement: The tides act as a check on our globe, and the rotation of the earth is becoming slower and slower.
propositions.quote: the tides act as a check on our globe, and that the rotation of the earth is becoming slower and slower

propositions.name: moon_apparent_acceleration_explained_by_earth_slowing
propositions.statement: The apparent acceleration of the motion of the moon is explained because our watch, which is the earth, is going slow.
propositions.quote: the apparent acceleration of the motion of the moon, which would seem to be going more rapidly than theory permits because our watch, which is the earth, is going slow

propositions.name: postulate_same_causes_same_time
propositions.statement: The same causes take the same time to produce the same effects.
propositions.quote: the same causes take the same time to produce the same effects

propositions.name: postulate_could_be_contradicted_by_experiment
propositions.statement: It is not impossible that experiment may some day contradict the postulate that the same causes take the same time to produce the same effects.
propositions.quote: Is it impossible that experiment may some day contradict our postulate?

propositions.name: multitude_of_causes_produce_effect
propositions.statement: In physical reality one cause does not produce a given effect, but a multitude of distinct causes contribute to produce it.
propositions.quote: one cause does not produce a given effect, but a multitude of distinct causes contribute to produce it

propositions.name: every_attraction_acts_on_pendulum
propositions.statement: In all rigor every attraction, even of Sirius, acts on the pendulum.
propositions.quote: in all rigor every attraction, even of Sirius, acts on the pendulum

propositions.name: revised_postulate_almost_identical_causes
propositions.statement: Causes almost identical take almost the same time to produce almost the same effects.
propositions.quote: Causes almost identical take almost the same time to produce almost the same effects.

propositions.name: earths_rotation_velocity_may_vary
propositions.statement: The velocity of the earth's rotation is a circumstance of any phenomenon, and if this velocity of rotation varies, the circumstance no longer remains the same.
propositions.quote: if this velocity of rotation varies, it constitutes in the reproduction of this phenomenon a circumstance which no longer remains the same

propositions.name: tidal_friction_destroys_vis_viva
propositions.statement: The friction of the tides producing heat must destroy vis viva.
propositions.quote: the friction of the tides producing heat must destroy vis viva

propositions.name: newtons_law_experimental_truth_approximate
propositions.statement: Newton’s law is an experimental truth, and as such it is only approximate.
propositions.quote: Newton’s law is an experimental truth; as such it is only approximate

propositions.name: star_conflagration_1572
propositions.statement: In 1572, Tycho Brahe noticed in the heavens a new star, caused by an immense conflagration that had happened in some far distant heavenly body.
propositions.quote: In 1572, Tycho Brahe noticed in the heavens a new star. An immense conflagration had happened in some far distant heavenly body

propositions.name: light_takes_time_to_travel_from_star
propositions.statement: At least two hundred years were necessary for the light from that star to reach our earth.
propositions.quote: at least two hundred years were necessary for the light from that star to reach our earth

propositions.name: cause_regarded_as_anterior_to_effect
propositions.statement: When a phenomenon appears to us as the cause of another, we regard it as anterior.
propositions.quote: when a phenomenon appears to us as the cause of another, we regard it as anterior

propositions.name: thunder_caused_by_electric_discharge
propositions.statement: On hearing thunder, we conclude there has been an electric discharge, and we consider the physical phenomenon as anterior to the auditory image.
propositions.quote: I hear thunder, and I conclude there has been an electric discharge; I do not hesitate to consider the physical phenomenon as anterior to the auditory image

propositions.name: sound_of_thunder_delayed_after_discharge
propositions.statement: We hear the sound of the thunder only some seconds after the electric discharge of the cloud.
propositions.quote: We hear the sound of the thunder only some seconds after the electric discharge of the cloud.

propositions.name: distant_lightning_may_precede_despite_later_sound
propositions.statement: Of two flashes of lightning, the distant one may be anterior to the near one even though the sound of the near one comes to us before that of the distant one.
propositions.quote: can not the first be anterior to the second, even though the sound of the second comes to us before that of the first?

propositions.name: universe_state_determines_phenomenon
propositions.statement: If all the parts of the universe are interchained, any one phenomenon is the resultant of causes infinitely numerous, the consequence of the state of the universe a moment before.
propositions.quote: any one phenomenon will not be the effect of a single cause, but the resultant of causes infinitely numerous; it is, one often says, the consequence of the state of the universe a moment before

propositions.name: three_body_positions_determine_future_positions
propositions.statement: The positions and the velocities of three bodies at a given instant suffice to determine their positions and velocities at the following instant, and consequently at any instant.
propositions.quote: The positions and the velocities of three bodies at a given instant suffice to determine their positions and velocities at the following instant, and consequently at any instant.

propositions.name: light_has_constant_velocity_same_in_all_directions
propositions.statement: Light has a constant velocity, and in particular its velocity is the same in all directions.
propositions.quote: He has begun by supposing that light has a constant velocity, and in particular that its velocity is the same in all directions.

propositions.name: roemer_measured_light_velocity_via_jupiter_eclipses
propositions.statement: Roemer used eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter, and sought how much the event fell behind its prediction, to measure the velocity of light.
propositions.quote: Roemer used eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter, and sought how much the event fell behind its prediction

propositions.name: moon_eclipse_not_perceived_instantaneously_everywhere
propositions.statement: An eclipse of the moon is not perceived exactly simultaneously from all points of the earth, since the propagation of light is not instantaneous.
propositions.quote: That is not altogether true, since the propagation of light is not instantaneous

propositions.name: telegraph_signal_received_after_sent
propositions.statement: The reception of the telegraph signal at Berlin is after the sending of this same signal from Paris.
propositions.quote: the reception of the signal at Berlin, for instance, is after the sending of this same signal from Paris

propositions.name: transmission_duration_nonzero_but_neglected
propositions.statement: The duration of the transmission of a signal is neglected and the two events are regarded as simultaneous, though a correction would in rigor be needed.
propositions.quote: In general, the duration of the transmission is neglected and the two events are regarded as simultaneous.

propositions.name: rules_of_simultaneity_chosen_for_convenience_not_truth
propositions.statement: The rules for simultaneity, order of succession, and equality of durations are chosen not because they are true, but because they are the most convenient.
propositions.quote: We therefore choose these rules, not because they are true, but because they are the most convenient
